Most abundant species per survey with TWINSPAN classification

Source: R/first_ten_species_twspn.R
first_ten_species_twspn.Rd

Rank the original abundance values within each survey and format the first species as text. Input orientation defaults to the surveys-by-species matrix accepted by ecan::twinspan().

Usage

first_ten_species_twspn(
  data_SRA_SC = NULL,
  join.dendrogram = TRUE,
  twin_ecan = NULL,
  n = 10,
  digits = 1,
  surveys.rows = TRUE,
  include.zero = FALSE
)

Arguments

data_SRA_SC

Numeric matrix or data.frame of abundances. By default, rows are surveys and columns are species. If NULL, use twin_ecan$data. Names on both dimensions must be unique and non-empty.

join.dendrogram

Logical; order surveys as in twin_ecan and include their positions and terminal groups?

twin_ecan

An object returned by ecan::twinspan(). Both classical and modified TWINSPAN are supported, including species = FALSE.

n

Positive integer; maximum number of species returned per survey.

digits

Non-negative integer; decimal places used in displayed values.

surveys.rows

Logical; if FALSE, data_SRA_SC has species in rows and surveys in columns, as in the original iPastoralist function. This argument applies only to explicitly supplied data, not twin_ecan$data.

include.zero

Logical; include absent species (zero abundance) after the present species?

Value

A data.frame with Survey, optionally cluster and Survey.order, and text columns X1, ..., Xn (for example, "Festuca rubra 12.5").

Details

Species are ordered by unrounded abundance, with ties resolved by input species order. Rounding is applied only to the displayed text. No conversion to percentages is performed. If fewer than n eligible species occur in a survey, its remaining entries are NA_character_.

Unlike the original function, the result always has one row per survey; no survey is dropped. With join.dendrogram = FALSE, rows follow the input order. When joining, all fitted survey IDs must be present exactly once. An explicit abundance table may use different units or species columns from the fitting matrix; only survey IDs are matched to the classification.

See also

denspe_twspn(), clustOrder_twspn()

Examples

veg <- rbind(S1 = c(9, 5, 0, 0), S2 = c(8, 4, 1, 0),
             S3 = c(0, 1, 5, 8), S4 = c(0, 0, 4, 7))
colnames(veg) <- c("Species A", "Species B", "Species C", "Species D")
tw <- ecan::twinspan(veg, modified = TRUE, n_clusters = 2,
                     min_size = 2, polish = "hill", species = FALSE)
first_ten_species_twspn(twin_ecan = tw, n = 3)
#>   Survey cluster Survey.order          X1          X2          X3
#> 1     S3       1            1 Species D 8 Species C 5 Species B 1
#> 2     S4       1            2 Species D 7 Species C 4        <NA>
#> 3     S1       2            3 Species A 9 Species B 5        <NA>
#> 4     S2       2            4 Species A 8 Species B 4 Species C 1
first_ten_species_twspn(veg, join.dendrogram = FALSE, n = 3)
#>   Survey          X1          X2          X3
#> 1     S1 Species A 9 Species B 5        <NA>
#> 2     S2 Species A 8 Species B 4 Species C 1
#> 3     S3 Species D 8 Species C 5 Species B 1
#> 4     S4 Species D 7 Species C 4        <NA>
first_ten_species_twspn(t(veg), twin_ecan = tw, surveys.rows = FALSE)
#>   Survey cluster Survey.order          X1          X2          X3   X4   X5
#> 1     S3       1            1 Species D 8 Species C 5 Species B 1 <NA> <NA>
#> 2     S4       1            2 Species D 7 Species C 4        <NA> <NA> <NA>
#> 3     S1       2            3 Species A 9 Species B 5        <NA> <NA> <NA>
#> 4     S2       2            4 Species A 8 Species B 4 Species C 1 <NA> <NA>
#>     X6   X7   X8   X9  X10
#> 1 <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA>
#> 2 <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA>
#> 3 <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA>
#> 4 <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA> <NA>
